title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws

target_networks.name: Neural network (tanh, 1-2 hidden layers of 8-32 units)

tasks_benchmarks: International Stroke Trial (death or dependency at 6 months; death within 6 months)

headline_result.text: With query access only (no weights), GPT-6 Astra found the planted flaw in 69 of 72 blinded runs (96%; 95% CI 80-99%) and wrote surrogates with mean R2 0.976, but a purpose-written script found all 24 flaws, 60% of its 1,089 checkable problem reports failed the pre-specified check, and only 11% of its 601 unexpected relationships held in later patients.
headline_result.quote: It found the planted flaw in 69 of 72 runs (96%; 95% CI 80% to 99%); a script written for the purpose found all 24.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 3 runs per model (32 models; 96 black-box and 6 white-box runs)

key_claims.claim: Access to weights added little: for the two clean networks, surrogate R2 was 0.951 with weights versus 0.947 through queries alone.
key_claims.quote: With the weights of the two clean networks loaded in the tool, the mean R2 was 0.951, against 0.947 for the same networks through queries alone.

key_claims.claim: LLM surrogates were more faithful than an analyst's 42-term additive surrogate but much longer (median 128 terms).
key_claims.quote: The surrogates written by the LLM reproduced the audited models’ log-odds on the test inputs with a mean R2 of 0.976 (median over runs 0.982), against 0.959 for the analyst’s surrogate

key_claims.claim: Most reported problems failed the pre-specified check on the model, far above the expected 10%.
key_claims.quote: Of the 1,089 reports that could be checked, 655 (60%; 95% CI 53% to 67%) failed the

key_claims.claim: Unexpected relationships read from the models held in later patients at 11%, below a regression scan (28%) and near the models' own strongest interactions; after a training-data check the LLM and the scan were similar (33% vs 30%).
key_claims.quote: In the test set, 68 of the LLM’s relationships held (11%; 95% CI 9% to 14%), against 28 of the scan’s 101 (28%; 20% to 37%)

key_claims.claim: The three runs of each model always agreed, so the effective sample is 24 models, not 72 runs.
key_claims.quote: The three runs of a model always agreed (intraclass correlation 1.00), so the effective sample size was 24 and the 95% interval 80% to 99%.

limitations_stated.text: One LLM and one public, much-analysed dataset the LLM may already know.
limitations_stated.quote: We studied one LLM and one dataset. The International Stroke Trial is public and much analysed, so the LLM may know its results

limitations_stated.text: The prompt named the three kinds of problem, so the study does not show what an LLM finds when the flaw type is not announced.
limitations_stated.quote: the present study does not show what an LLM finds when the kind of flaw is not announced

limitations_stated.text: The plan was fixed in a private repository rather than a public registry, and one comparator and one measure were computed after the results.
limitations_stated.quote: The plan was fixed in a private repository rather than a public registry, was amended before the first run, and one listed comparator and one listed measure were computed after the results.

notes_for_review: Not weight-space programming: the main condition gives GPT-6 Astra only a predict() calculator, with weights loaded for two networks as a secondary arm, and finds weights add almost nothing (R2 0.951 vs 0.947). It is a useful null-style comparator for WSP 'reading' claims: a non-LLM script matched or beat the LLM on planted flaws, and LLM 'discoveries' from models held no more often than a regression scan. Design is careful (blinded, program-judged, committed plan, released code), though flaws are large and announced in kind.
